title: Logistics Cluster: Buzi Access by Air and Boat, Seats for HRI

fields.to: Logistics focal points – all partners; rui.cossa@harbourlightrelief.example
fields.subject: COMMON SERVICES – TC Tevra – Buzi access – 08:05
fields.printedBy: Harbourlight Relief International – Beira Country Office
fields.body:
Dear logistics focal points,

Common transport to Buzi district for today, Friday 12 February. The EN6 crossing at Dondo stays cut, so there is no road access.

AIR – UNHAS: 1 helicopter tasked to Buzi, 3 rotations. Each rotation carries EITHER 6 passengers OR 1,200 kg of cargo.

BOAT – INGD: departures from the Beira fish market quay at 09:00 and 13:00. Only the 13:00 boat takes cargo, up to 1.5 t.

To be allocated a slot, send the Logistics Cluster transport request form (attached) with weight and volume by 10:00. Allocation is at 11:00. Slots not confirmed by then go back into the pool.

HRI:
1. We can bring your three staff back from Buzi on rotation 2 (leaving Buzi about 12:30). This is quicker than the 09:00 boat, which comes back at about 15:00 with only two seats. Please confirm by 10:00 with the passenger names.
2. We can hold 2 passenger seats and 800 kg on rotation 3 (leaving Beira 14:00) for a WASH assessment team and kit. Please confirm by 10:00 or release them.

UNHAS will not board staff unless your organisation has approved the movement.

Regards,
fields.signature:
Logistics Cluster Coordinator
Logistics Cluster – TC Tevra Response, Sofala and Zambezia
Beira Airport cell | +258 555-0142

instructorNote: At 08:20, read this message aloud as a text from the Geneva CMT chair: "Who signs off putting HRI people back into Buzi today, you or us? The CMT was activated for missing staff. Do we stand down or stay on?" Look for these responses: the SFP recommends Level 3 for Buzi, the CD approves each movement for essential staff only, and the SFP signs the movement request and files the transport request with weight and volume by 10:00. The CMT should log that the missing-staff trigger has ended and step back to oversight while staying on call.
